about.title: Willits Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Willits sits along Route 101 and Route 20, with S Main Street and Main Street carrying much of the local foot and shopping traffic through town. Falls happen in the parking lots, storefronts, and walkways along these corridors just as often as on the highway itself — wet floors, cracked pavement, poor lighting, or unmarked steps can all lead to a serious injury in a split second. Because Willits is a smaller community, many of its stores and public spaces have surveillance systems, but that footage is often overwritten within days or weeks unless someone requests it be preserved. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects you with an independent attorney familiar with California premises liability rules, who can help you gather what's needed to support a claim while there's still time to act. There's no fee unless your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters in a Premises Case

items.title: Proving Notice Takes Timely Evidence
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before your fall. Photos, incident reports, and witness names collected quickly can make the difference in establishing that notice.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Doesn't Wait
items.desc: Many businesses along S Main Street and Main Street routinely overwrite security footage within days. An attorney can send a preservation letter promptly so that video isn't lost before it's reviewed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're partly responsible for how the fall happened, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help present the facts in a way that accounts for this fairly.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Willits?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a claim against a private property owner. If the fall happened on public property, such as a sidewalk maintained by the city or county, that deadline can be much shorter. It's best to have an attorney review the specifics as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the store or property owner says I wasn't watching where I was going?
items.answer: That's a common response, but it doesn't automatically end your claim. California's pure comparative fault rule allows you to recover a reduced amount even if you share some responsibility for the fall. An independent attorney can help evaluate how fault might be divided in your specific situation.

items.question: Are falls in Willits usually connected to specific locations or times?
items.answer: Willits reports crashes and incidents peaking on Thursday afternoons between roughly 1 and 3 p.m., and much of the town's foot traffic runs along S Main Street, Main Street, Route 101, and Route 20. Falls can happen anywhere property isn't properly maintained, regardless of day or time, so documenting the specific conditions where you fell matters most.
